h1: The 8 Best Ice Makers Under $200, Nugget and Bullet Countertop Models, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ice Maker Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 countertop ice makers under $200, nugget and bullet styles, scored on daily output, ice type, finish and cleaning features.
summary: The Frigidaire Crunchy Chewable Nugget Ice Maker V2 is the best ice maker under $200 for nugget lovers, making 33 lbs a day in a gunmetal body. The EUHOMY stainless nugget machine adds self-cleaning, and the Frigidaire and hOmeLabs bullet makers are the lower-bracket options for plain cubes.
intro: Two hundred dollars splits the ice maker market neatly in half. Below about $100 you buy bullet ice, the hard, hollow cubes every countertop machine makes. Above it, you start to see nugget ice, the soft pellets that people line up for at drive-throughs. The question is not which machine is better but which kind of ice you actually want in your glass.

Eight machines are ranked below, three nugget makers and five bullet makers. Scoring covers daily output, ice type, build, cleaning features and listing detail. Output numbers are the makers' own best-case figures, so expect less in a warm kitchen.

products.name: Frigidaire Crunchy Chewable Nugget Ice Maker V2
products.verdict: Chewable nugget ice at 33 lbs a day from a major appliance brand, in a gunmetal finish.
products.description:
The Frigidaire Crunchy Chewable V2 makes nugget ice at up to 33 lbs a day on a countertop body with a gunmetal finish. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Nugget ice is porous, so it soaks up the flavour of the drink and gives way when you chew, which is why people pay extra for it. Frigidaire is a major appliance name, and that means easier warranty claims and a wider service network than most sellers offer at this price. It takes first place on that blend of ice style and brand support.

Buy it if you want chewable ice from a known name. Skip it if you want clear cubes for cocktails.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker Countertop Stainless Steel
products.verdict: Stainless steel nugget maker at 35 lbs a day, on a 7-minute cycle with self-cleaning.
products.description:
The stainless EUHOMY produces 35 lbs per 24 hours on a 7-minute cycle, with a self-cleaning routine, a scoop and a basket.

Its edge over the Frigidaire is a documented cleaning cycle and a little more output. The stainless body resists dents and stains better than painted plastic. The cost is a listing with no warranty detail and a less familiar brand.

Buy it if self-cleaning and output matter most. Skip it if you prefer a household-name brand.
products.idealFor: Nugget fans who want low-fuss care.

products.name: Kismile Nugget Ice Maker Countertop
products.verdict: A 35 lb a day stainless nugget maker, but light on listed details.
products.description:
The Kismile makes up to 35 lbs of nugget ice a day in a stainless steel countertop body.

Output matches the EUHOMY stainless, which makes it a competitor on paper. It ranks third because the listing gives no cycle time, no cleaning mode and no accessories, so the buying case rests on the headline number.

Buy it if you want a stainless nugget maker and can compare prices. Skip it if you want the cleaning feature confirmed.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker Countertop with Handle
products.verdict: 34 lbs a day on a 6-minute cycle, with a removable top cover and auto-cleaning.
products.description:
This EUHOMY nugget maker offers 34 lbs per day on a 6-minute cycle, with a removable top cover, auto-cleaning, a basket and a scoop.

The removable cover is the practical detail: it opens up the inside for a proper wipe, which most sealed machines do not allow. It ranks fourth because output is slightly below the stainless version and the plastic body is plainer.

Buy it if you want to move the machine and clean it easily. Skip it if you prefer a metal body.

products.name: hOmeLabs Countertop Ice Maker
products.verdict: Bullet ice, nine cubes per six minutes and up to 26 lbs a day, in the lower bracket.
products.description:
The hOmeLabs makes nine cubes every six minutes, up to 26 lbs in a day, on a countertop body in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It is the plain choice for people who only want ice and do not care about nugget. The listing says little about cleaning or accessories, so ranking depends on the output numbers and brand history.

Buy it if you want ordinary cubes cheaply. Skip it if you want nugget ice.
products.idealFor: Basic cubes at the lowest cost.

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC117 Stainless Steel Ice Maker
products.verdict: A compact Frigidaire with a copper stainless finish and 26 lbs a day.
products.description:
The EFIC117 is a compact countertop ice maker with a copper stainless finish and 26 lbs per day of output.

The finish is the point: it looks like a small appliance rather than a plastic gadget. It ranks sixth because the listing is silent on cycle time and cleaning, and it only matches the output of cheaper bullet makers.

Buy it if looks matter. Skip it if you want specs.

products.name: FRIGIDAIRE Retro Compact Ice Maker
products.verdict: White retro styling, bullet ice and 26 lbs a day.
products.description:
The Frigidaire Retro makes bullet ice at 26 lbs a day in a white body with retro styling.

It fits the vintage-kitchen trend and does the job of a basic bullet maker. It ranks seventh because the retro looks cost more than they add to performance, and the listing gives no cleaning details.

Buy it if your kitchen has a retro theme. Skip it if you want features.

products.name: Frigidaire 26 Lbs Portable Compact Ice Maker
products.verdict: A medium-size stainless finish machine producing 26 lbs a day.
products.description:
This Frigidaire is a portable compact ice maker with a stainless finish, medium size and 26 lbs a day.

It ranks last because it is the least distinct: the same output as the others, no listed cycle time and no cleaning detail. It is a fine low-risk option if you want the Frigidaire name.

Buy it if you want a no-surprises brand. Skip it if you want any standout feature.

whatMatters.detail: Nugget ice is soft and chewable and absorbs flavour. Bullet ice is hard and keeps drinks cold longer. Nugget makers cost more and are louder. Decide on texture first.
The 26 to 35 lb range means roughly one to one and a half pounds an hour. That suits a household. For parties, freeze extra in bags beforehand.
A removable top and a self-cleaning cycle keep the reservoir fresh. Standing water grows slime, so empty it when not in use.
Stainless looks premium and resists staining. Nugget makers make a grinding noise while producing. Place them away from where you sit.
Major brands such as Frigidaire offer easier claims. Lesser-known sellers can be slower. Check the warranty length.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you love chewing ice or want drinks that soak up flavour, yes. If you only want cold drinks, bullet ice is cheaper and fine.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Ignoring cleaning. A machine you cannot open or flush grows slime. Check for a cleaning cycle or removable cover.

faq.q: Is the Frigidaire worth it over a lesser-known nugget maker?
faq.a: For brand support and warranty ease, yes. The EUHOMY adds documented self-cleaning for similar money.

faq.q: How long to the first ice?
faq.a: Around six to seven minutes for the first batch, once the water has chilled. A full basket takes an hour or more.
Nugget makers crush and extrude ice, which is louder than bullet makers. Place it away from living areas.
Monthly in hard-water areas, using a citric acid solution as the manual says.

finalTake: The Frigidaire Crunchy Chewable Nugget Ice Maker V2 is the best ice maker under $200 for those who want soft, chewable ice from a major brand. The EUHOMY stainless nugget model is the pick for self-cleaning, and the hOmeLabs is the cheapest cube maker. Decide on ice type, then check the cleaning design.
